territorial_scope.description: Applies to responsible parties domiciled in South Africa and to non-domiciled responsible parties that use automated or non-automated means in the Republic.

evidence.quote: not domiciled in the Republic, but makes use of automated or non-automated means in the Republic

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Protection of Personal Information Act 2013, assented 19 November 2013, regulates processing of personal information by responsible parties domiciled in or using means in South Africa. It sets eight processing conditions, limits on special and child information, automated decisions and transborder transfers, and Information Regulator enforcement with offences and fines.
summary.long: The Act regulates the processing of personal information by responsible parties domiciled in South Africa or using automated or non-automated means in it, and excludes purely personal or household activity, fully de-identified data, and certain journalistic, national security and judicial processing. Chapter 3 sets eight conditions: accountability, lawfulness and minimality with consent or other grounds, purpose specification, further processing limits, information quality, openness and notice, security safeguards with breach notification, and data subject participation. Part B prohibits processing special personal information and Part C prohibits processing children's personal information, each subject to listed authorisations or exceptions. Chapter 6 requires prior authorisation from the Regulator for listed processing. Chapter 8 regulates unsolicited electronic direct marketing and section 71 limits decisions based solely on automated profiling. Section 72 limits transfers outside the Republic. Chapter 5 establishes the Information Regulator, which may investigate, issue information and enforcement notices, and refer matters to an Enforcement Committee. Chapter 10 provides civil damages actions. Chapter 11 sets offences punishable by fines or imprisonment of up to 10 years or 12 months, and administrative fines not exceeding R10 million, which the Minister may adjust under section 109(10). The annotated part ends at section 109.

notes: This part covers the Act's text from the front matter through s.109(10). Section 110 (Amendment of laws), ss.111-115 and the amendment schedule are not in this extract and are left to part 2, so no amends or amended_by relations are coded here. The 'SCHEDULE: Laws amended by section 110' heading in this extract is followed by Chapter 1 text of this Act, which looks like a layout artefact. No internal inconsistency of substance was found. target_instrument_id is empty for every relation because none of the cited Acts is identified in the registry text; target_text carries the names. s.109(10) allows the Minister to adjust the s.109(2)(c) fine ceiling by notice; the R10 million ceiling is the figure in s.109(2)(c). Part 2 of 2 covers ss 110 to 115 and the Schedule. Schedule amendments to the Promotion of Access to Information Act restate amended text with brackets and strike-throughs; only the added or changed wording is relevant to coding. Target instrument IDs are not given in the text, so target_instrument_id is empty. Section 110 gives 'the third column of the Schedule' as the extent of the amendments.
